content:
Eva G.: Heads-up — multiple Dedicated customers in na-west2 (notably Acme Analytics) reporting increased 5xx + tail latency for text-generation endpoints since ~07:15 UTC. Symptoms: auth failures, placement retries, and high token billing spikes reported by their app.
Sam K.: Seeing the same in observability — per-route latency SLO breached, autoscaler logged repeated placement failures. I have an aggregation of errors, pushing below.

infra-bot: [07:18 UTC] autoscaler: placement_failure(zone=na-west2-a, reason=InsufficientGPU, attempts=3)
infra-bot: [07:19 UTC] scheduler: queue_backpressure(trigger=high_pending, threshold=85%)

Julia (support): Customer reports these errors in their app logs: `grpc: authentication handshake failed: token invalid` and `500: model_unavailable` intermittently. They see the errors spike when they run burst workloads (long chains).

Ryan (oncall): Copy. Adding quick triage notes: 1) Is this a GPU stockout or a noisy neighbor causing eviction/backpressure? 2) Did any autoscaler policy change/deploy in last hour? 3) Any cross-region fallback attempts that might cause auth/cert mismatches?

Sam K.: Checking deploy history — a config for autoscaler thresholds rolled out at 06:58 by canary, but rollout completed normally (deploy-bot shows success). No explicit capacity commit for na-west2.

deploy-bot: [06:58 UTC] autoscaler-config v2.14 promoted: reduced max-burst and more aggressive bin-packing. Canary passed.

Sam K.: The aggressive bin-packing looks like it reduced buffer capacity; combined with a few large tenants burst, we saw placement failures. Also seeing repeated `InstancePreempted` events in the nodepool logs — suggests noisy tenant preempting smaller reservations.

Eva G.: Repro steps from customer: 1) open a long streaming chat with 8 concurrent sessions; 2) run a heavy prompt (10k tokens); 3) after ~30s many sessions get 500 + `auth token invalid` on retry. They tried renewing their token — sometimes that clears it for a minute then it reappears.

Julia (support): I asked for the customer correlation id. They sent back trace_id=corr-0a9f. Attaching their request IDs below.

ML Platform: Correlating trace_id=corr-0a9f — we see requests routed to host pool `dedicated-na-west2-pool-3` then failed placement -> fallback routing to `dedicated-na-west1-fallback` which is in a different account alias. Fallback succeeded but returned `401` due to token audience mismatch (we do audience check per-region). That explains the intermittent auth errors.

Ryan (oncall): Perfect find. So chain is: oversubscribe/placement fail in na-west2 -> fallback to na-west1 -> token audience mismatch -> 401 -> client retries -> hits queue/backpressure -> 500. That matches customer report.

Sam K.: Mitigation options: 1) Temporarily increase buffer_capacity for na-west2 (hotfix) to absorb bursts. 2) Throttle heavy tenants at gateway (per-tenant concurrent limit). 3) Disable cross-region fallback until we patch audience handling for fallbacks. Which do we want now?

Eva G.: Customer impact urgent. I'd vote: (A) increase buffer for na-west2 immediately, (B) apply tenant throttles for top 3 noisy tenants (identify list), (C) disable fallback briefly so their auth errors stop. We'll need a rollout window.

Julia (support): I'll notify Acme that we're actively mitigating: raising capacity and applying temporary throttles. Also confirm their app can handle a brief fallback disable.

Ryan (oncall): I'll perform the buffer increase and disable fallback for na-west2 for 15 minutes, monitor traces. Sam, can you prepare throttling rules for top noisy tenants (based on last 24h token consumption)?

Sam K.: On it — running query: `SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) FROM usage WHERE region='na-west2' AND ts > now()-24h GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY SUM(tokens) DESC LIMIT 10;` Should have list in ~2 min.

infra-bot: [07:30 UTC] capacity: buffer_capacity(na-west2) scaled +30% (temp) by Ryan (oncall).

Ryan (oncall): Disabled cross-region fallback for na-west2. Monitoring.

Sam K.: Top tenants: tenant-987 (Acme's prod), tenant-102, tenant-221. Draft throttles: concurrent_streams cap 6, token_rate_limit 1200/s for those tenants. I will apply caps for 30m and iterate.

Eva G.: Julia, please coordinate with Acme and set expectation: we might see higher latency for a short window but fewer 5xx/401s.

Julia (support): Noted. Messaging now.

ML Platform: After buffer scale and throttle, placement failure rate decreased by 80% in na-west2. No further `401` fallbacks observed. Customer reports reduced errors.

Eva G.: Good. Next steps: 1) root cause: autoscaler bin-packing change + uncommitted capacity -> insufficient headroom. 2) follow-up: revert aggressive bin-packing change or add a safety buffer for Dedicated regions. 3) permanent fix: make fallback handle token audience or perform token translation so cross-region fallback doesn't 401. 4) consider quota/limits UI to warn customers about burst risks.

Ryan (oncall): I'll open an incident ticket for postmortem and assign to Eng-Platform + Autoscaler team. Also recommend we schedule a brief emergency capacity commit for na-west2 if forecast shows recurring bursts.

Sam K.: Adding repro logs and a short script in the incident ticket to reproduce locally (uses k8s test harness + synthetic tenant bursts). Recommend running overnight load test with new autoscaler config toggles.

Julia (support): Acme confirmed services stabilized. They asked for a timeline for fallback fix — I'll say 2 weeks for an engineering patch and a config change in the meantime.

Eva G.: Thanks all. I'll draft the incident summary and postmortem. If anyone sees a regression ping here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [07:57 UTC] autoscaler-config rollback queued (pending review).

Ryan (oncall): Marking this thread resolved for now. Last observed customer error at 07:42 UTC.

Eva G.: Closing when postmortem created."
